newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse pursues cautious upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse pursues cautious upward trend.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.49 percent higher lifted by gains in ONA group while its subsidiary Financiere Diwan accounted for the main trade on the official market with 4,769 shares exchanged, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 640.21 points from 637.07 points on Wednesday.
ONA, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, gained 15 dirhams to 795 dirhams., was unchanged at 330 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid rose five dirhams to 550 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Wafabank gained eight dirhams to 824 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur edged up one dirham to 580 dirhams.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams.
SNI, the second largest private group, dipped two dirhams to 730 dirhams.
In the energy sector, Samir fell four dirhams to 351 dirhams. Mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter dropped 15 dirhams to 561 dirhams.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996, fell 18 dirhams to 1,370 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 27.6 from 12.1 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 30.5 million from 137.4 million dirhams. Samir had 3,667 shares traded, followed by 2,104 SMI and 2,000 ONA.
